reason: Re-examined transitive proof route after the finite corner-sector construction was made explicit for reflex as well as convex ordinary corners. Full Lee Chapter 9, Datar Lectures 1–2, Jost §2.3.A and Wendl §6.3 were inspected; current direct prerequisites are listed in dependencies. Proof strategy: Interpolate g_t=(1−t)g₀+tg₁. On a finite disk cover, apply the positive g₀-to-g_t square-root bundle map to a fixed oriented g₀-frame; the resulting g_t-frames have the same SO(2) transition functions for all t. Hence β=ω₁−ω₀ glues to a global 1-form in the oriented case, and dω=−K dA gives K₁dA₁−K₀dA₀=−dβ. Stokes makes the curvature-integral change −∫∂Mβ. Along each fixed regular boundary arc, the angle formula gives (k₁ds₁−k₀ds₀)=d(θ₁−θ₀)+β. The angle difference has a single-valued lift through the metric path; its total derivative over closed boundary components plus its finite corner jumps is zero. Each corner jump difference is exactly α₁−α₀, so the boundary and corner change is +∫∂Mβ and cancels. On a closed nonorientable surface use a fixed finite disk triangulation from the first metric, choose each face orientation separately, perform the same β computation on its faces, and pair interior-edge integrals: reversal of face orientation changes both β and its integration orientation, leaving opposite inward conormals and cancellation. No classification, Euler–Poincaré theorem or later characteristic-form theory is used.
